title: Earth System Trend Detective

methods.anomalies: Monthly values minus the average for the same calendar month, so seasons do not look like trends.
methods.rate: Sen slope (median of all pairwise slopes) per decade with a 95% confidence interval.
methods.tests: Mann-Kendall test with the variance inflated for month-to-month autocorrelation (lag-1), or an OLS t-test when the residuals pass Durbin-Watson and Shapiro checks (in practice Mann-Kendall was used for every variable).
methods.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate at 5%: across cells for maps, across the 11 spotlight regions for each variable, and separately across the IPCC regions (the global mean is one separate test).
methods.effect_size: Total change over the record divided by the month-to-month noise (SD of detrended anomalies).

caveats: Twenty years is short; trends can reflect natural variability such as El Niño, not only long-term change.
The Mann-Kendall correction is slightly liberal (about 6% false positives at a nominal 5% in simulation).
A 5° grid smooths small regions: a box smaller than a cell is averaged over the whole cell.
Hotspots are chosen because their cells look significant, so their p-values are optimistic (exploratory).
Land models disagree with each other for some variables; this is shown, not hidden.
Variables were selected by a data-driven method plus six hand-picked headline variables; see 'role'.
not_available: AIRS products, MOD21C3 and tropospheric ozone were not used. Snow cover has 238 of 240 months.

variables.name: Near-surface air temperature
variables.definition: Air temperature about 2 m above the ground or sea surface. It comes from MERRA-2, a global model that blends satellite and ground observations.
variables.source: MERRA-2 monthly means (M2TMNXSLV), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.224 °C per decade (statistically significant); 31% of the area has a significant trend (30% rising, 1% falling).

variables.name: Sea surface temperature
variables.definition: Temperature of the top layer of the ocean, a reconstruction (ERSST v5) from ship, buoy and satellite-era records on a 2° grid.
variables.source: ERSST v5 (NOAA NCDC) as distributed by NASA PO.DAAC (REYNOLDS_NCDC_L4_MONTHLY_V5)
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.223 °C per decade (statistically significant); 28% of the area has a significant trend (28% rising, 0% falling).

variables.name: Sea level (height anomaly)
variables.definition: How much higher or lower the sea surface is than its long-term average, measured by satellite radar altimeters.
variables.source: NASA-SSH Simple Gridded Sea Surface Height v1.1 (NASA PO.DAAC)
variables.finding: Globally rising by 3.57 cm per decade (statistically significant); 83% of the area has a significant trend (83% rising, 0% falling).

variables.name: Precipitation rate
variables.definition: How much rain and snow falls, averaged per day, from a merged estimate of satellite microwave and infrared sensors with rain-gauge correction.
variables.source: GPM IMERG monthly (GPM_3IMERGM), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.0225 mm/day per decade (not significant on its own); 17% of the area has a significant trend (8% rising, 9% falling).

variables.name: Snow cover
variables.definition: The share of each grid cell that is covered by snow in a month, from MODIS on the Terra satellite (0 to 100%).
variables.source: MODIS/Terra Snow Cover Monthly L3 Global 0.05° (MOD10CM), NASA NSIDC DAAC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.221 % of area per decade (statistically significant); 2% of the area has a significant trend (1% rising, 1% falling).

variables.name: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
variables.definition: An index of how green and dense plant cover is. Higher values mean more healthy vegetation; bare ground and water are near zero or below.
variables.source: MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices Monthly L3 Global 0.05° (MOD13C2), NASA LP DAAC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.00801 index per decade (statistically significant); 34% of the area has a significant trend (32% rising, 2% falling).

variables.name: Terrestrial water storage
variables.definition: All the water held on land (soil water, groundwater, snow and surface water), as simulated by a land model. In mm of water.
variables.source: GLDAS Catchment land model monthly (GLDAS_CLSM10_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 29.4 mm of water per decade (not significant on its own); 8% of the area has a significant trend (1% rising, 7% falling).

variables.name: Sunlight reaching the surface
variables.definition: Incoming shortwave (solar) energy that reaches the ground or sea, averaged over the month.
variables.source: MERRA-2 monthly radiation (M2TMNXRAD), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.899 W/m² per decade (statistically significant); 22% of the area has a significant trend (4% rising, 18% falling).

variables.name: Surface soil wetness
variables.definition: How full of water the top soil layer is, from 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated).
variables.source: MERRA-2 land surface (M2TMNXLND), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.00172 fraction (0–1) per decade (statistically significant); 4% of the area has a significant trend (3% rising, 1% falling).

variables.name: Sunlight absorbed by land
variables.definition: Net shortwave (solar) energy absorbed by the land surface: incoming sunlight minus what is reflected.
variables.source: GLDAS VIC land model monthly (GLDAS_VIC10_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 1.9 W/m² per decade (not significant on its own); 34% of the area has a significant trend (30% rising, 4% falling).

variables.name: Aerosol optical depth
variables.definition: How much sunlight is blocked by tiny airborne particles such as dust, smoke, sea salt and pollution. Higher means hazier air.
variables.source: MERRA-2 aerosol diagnostics (M2TMNXAER), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.000971 index per decade (not significant on its own); 44% of the area has a significant trend (26% rising, 18% falling).

variables.name: Soil moisture, 10–40 cm
variables.definition: Water held in the soil layer 10 to 40 cm below the surface (1 kg per m² is about 1 mm of water).
variables.source: GLDAS Noah land model 0.25° monthly (GLDAS_NOAH025_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.687 kg/m² per decade (not significant on its own); 27% of the area has a significant trend (10% rising, 17% falling).

variables.name: Height of the 500 hPa level
variables.definition: The altitude (about 5.5 km) where air pressure is 500 hPa. It rises when the air column below warms, so it tracks warming of the lower atmosphere.
variables.source: MERRA-2 monthly means (M2TMNXSLV), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 7.15 m per decade (statistically significant); 65% of the area has a significant trend (65% rising, 0% falling).

variables.name: Latent heat flux (evaporation energy)
variables.definition: Energy that leaves the land surface as water evaporates. Higher means more evaporation and plant water use.
variables.source: GLDAS Catchment land model monthly (GLDAS_CLSM10_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.383 W/m² per decade (not significant on its own); 20% of the area has a significant trend (11% rising, 9% falling).

variables.name: Cloud-top temperature
variables.definition: Temperature at the top of the clouds. Colder tops mean taller clouds.
variables.source: MERRA-2 monthly means (M2TMNXSLV), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.198 K per decade (statistically significant); 2% of the area has a significant trend (1% rising, 0% falling).

variables.name: Storm surface runoff
variables.definition: Rain water that runs over the ground surface instead of soaking in (accumulated amount, as provided by the model).
variables.source: GLDAS VIC land model monthly (GLDAS_VIC10_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.00402 kg/m² (≈ mm) per decade (statistically significant); 17% of the area has a significant trend (4% rising, 13% falling).

variables.name: Evapotranspiration (land)
variables.definition: Water returned to the air from soil and plants, averaged per day.
variables.source: FLDAS Noah land model monthly (FLDAS_NOAH01_C_GL_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.00741 mm/day per decade (not significant on its own); 18% of the area has a significant trend (13% rising, 5% falling).

variables.name: Soil temperature, top 10 cm
variables.definition: Temperature of the top 10 cm of the soil.
variables.source: GLDAS Noah land model 0.25° monthly (GLDAS_NOAH025_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally rising by 0.104 °C per decade (not significant on its own); 42% of the area has a significant trend (19% rising, 23% falling).

variables.name: Soil moisture, VIC middle layer
variables.definition: Water held in the second (middle) soil layer of the VIC land model (1 kg per m² is about 1 mm of water).
variables.source: GLDAS VIC land model monthly (GLDAS_VIC10_M), NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 4.86 kg/m² per decade (statistically significant); 12% of the area has a significant trend (2% rising, 9% falling).

variables.name: Surface evaporation
variables.definition: Water evaporating from the surface into the air, averaged per day (negative values are dew or condensation).
variables.source: MERRA-2 surface flux diagnostics (M2TMNXFLX), NASA GMAO, via NASA GES DISC
variables.finding: Globally falling by 0.0424 mm/day per decade (statistically significant); 20% of the area has a significant trend (6% rising, 14% falling).

regions.name: Amazon Basin
regions.blurb: The largest rainforest on Earth. Rainfall, greenness and water storage here affect weather far away.

regions.name: Sahel
regions.blurb: The dry belt south of the Sahara, where rain and plant growth are closely linked.

regions.name: Arctic Ocean (Alaska side)
regions.blurb: Sea ice and cold ocean, where warming shows up fastest.

regions.name: Tibetan Plateau
regions.blurb: High ground that stores snow and feeds the great rivers of Asia.

regions.name: Great Barrier Reef
regions.blurb: A coral reef system that is very sensitive to sea temperature.

regions.name: North Sea & Low Countries
regions.blurb: A busy, densely populated coast: air, rain and sea all in one box.

regions.name: California Central Valley
regions.blurb: A major farming region that depends on snowmelt and irrigation.

regions.name: Mediterranean Basin
regions.blurb: A climate hotspot: hotter summers and less rain are expected here.

regions.name: Indonesia & Maritime Southeast Asia
regions.blurb: Tropical islands with heavy rain, forest change and seasonal smoke.

regions.name: Indo-Gangetic Plain (northern India)
regions.blurb: One of the most densely populated plains on Earth, with heavy air pollution.

regions.name: Antarctic Peninsula
regions.blurb: The part of Antarctica that points toward South America and warms quickly.
